title: Unit 7 rem early — armor as Christ; wrestling not against flesh
english: written, one can say that the whole armor of God is Christ, so that "Put on the whole armor of God" is the same as "Put on the Lord Jesus Christ" (Romans 13:14). For if the belt is truth and the breastplate is righteousness, and the Savior is the truth and the righteousness, it is clear that the Savior is the belt and the breastplate. In the same way he himself would be the readiness of the gospel of peace, and the shield of faith, and the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God: the Word who is living and active and sharper than any two-edged sword (Hebrews 4:12).

What other whole armor of God could one even imagine being meant, which the one who will stand against the schemes of the devil must put on, except virtue, which is Christ? For whoever has put him on, in all his aspects, will be able to stand against all the schemes of wickedness that are worked by its father, the devil. Insofar as someone has girded himself with truth, he will not be dragged into assenting to persuasive and sophistical arguments made on behalf of falsehood. Insofar as he has clothed himself with righteousness, he will be unwounded by the arrows of unrighteousness, since none of them gets through to make the one who has put on righteousness unrighteous.

And the one who has bound on the fine shoes of the readiness of the gospel of peace, being ready and having made his works ready for the departure, and having therefore become a man of peace, will neither do anything warlike or factious nor be condemned along with the unready. Unbelief, the enemy of the salvation of the human race, will have no room where the shield of faith is. And the one who has the helmet of salvation set about his head will keep unbroken the head of the soul, where the divine senses of the mind are. More than that, like a noble soldier, the one who holds the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of the Lord, will cut down and destroy every teaching that is at war with the truth.

"For our wrestling is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the world rulers of the darkness, against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places" (Ephesians 6:12). I think that wrestling against blood and flesh means what he calls elsewhere human temptations (1 Corinthians 10:13), when the flesh, desiring against the spirit, calls us to do its works. But it is no longer a human temptation, nor wrestling against blood and flesh, when Satan, disguising himself as an angel of light (2 Corinthians 11:14), strives to persuade us to heed him as an angel of light; or when something like this happens, which comes about with all power and signs and lying wonders, and with all the deceit of unrighteousness (2 Thessalonians 2:9-10).

And if the enemy should persuade someone to receive him as the Lord, who will say within him, "Thus says the Lord," so that the person even supposes he has become a prophet of the God of all things, the enemy would do this not as blood and flesh, nor as a human temptation, but as one wrestling with a man who has guarded himself up to that point. That is why no place at all must be given to the devil.

Someone will say that "Our wrestling is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers, against the authorities," and the rest, is said to teach us not to think that even the sins which seem to come to us from the mind of the flesh come to us first from flesh and blood, but from certain powers that work them. For there are demons that work love affairs and love potions, as the prophet also shows when he says, "They were led astray by a spirit of fornication" (Hosea 4:12). The same may be said of other demons that stir up rage and anger; by calling on them, the dabblers in magic are said to make a charm for holding down anger. And when we hate, we do not hate without the demons who work hatred; one could argue this, not unreasonably, from the so-called hate charms.

"Since, then, the apostle wants to teach us," he says, "that sinning does not come to us from the nature of the body, he says for this reason, 'Our wrestling is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers, against the authorities,' and the rest." And as we ask what ancient Scriptures, revealed and made plain to him, Paul drew on in saying this, we conjecture that it came from the accounts of wars and single combats, such as David's fight against Goliath, and the fights of the sons of Israel against the foreigners or the nations they contended with and conquered. title: Unit 7 rem mid — evil day; belt, breastplate, shoes, shield
english: is, then, against authorities that are not visible or made of flesh; against world rulers of the darkness that surrounds the human race; and against the spirits of wickedness that dwell in the heavenly place, that is, the air. Elsewhere, at any rate, he said, "in which you once walked, according to the course of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, the spirit now at work in the [sons of] disobedience" (Ephesians 2:2). For the air poured around us seems to be filled with opposing powers.

"So that you may be able to withstand," he says, "in the evil day" (Ephesians 6:13). Origen: Whoever seeks to withstand in the evil day must have the whole armor of God that the apostle set out. Because of it the opponent will be put to shame, having nothing bad to say about us (Titus 2:8): the devil, the accuser of our brothers (Revelation 12:10), who deceives sinners as his own, as men who have come to belong to his portion. Another will say that the present age is the evil day. A third interpretation, besides these two, will say that the struggle has no end for the one who has left this life: even the one who has conquered here will have to contend in another evil day against the opposing forces that appear.

"Stand, therefore, having girded your waist with truth" (Ephesians 6:14). In Luke too it is written, "Let your waists be girded" (Luke 12:35). We know what the belt is here: the one who has curbed the business of begetting, and no longer serves it but hastens toward immortality, girds his waist.

"And having put on the breastplate of righteousness" (Ephesians 6:14). The one who has put on a breastplate is harder to hurt when enemies shoot at him, and hardest to hurt in the vital parts. In the same way the one clothed with righteousness could not be wounded, not even like a deer struck by an arrow in the liver. For he will fall neither into rage nor into desire, but will remain pure in heart, because he has put on the breastplate of righteousness forged for him by God, the craftsman of all things, who makes the whole armor for each of the saints and gives it to him.

"And having shod your feet with the readiness of the gospel of peace" (Ephesians 6:15). Observe that he has called a certain power of the soul "feet," with which, as it were, we travel, walking along the one who said, "I am the way" (John 14:6). These must be shod with the readiness of the gospel of peace. I think the shoes recorded in Exodus are symbols of these shoes, the ones that those who ate the Passover had to wear, being ready for the journey. For it says, "This is how you shall eat it: your waists girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staffs in your hands; and you shall eat it in haste. It is the Lord's Passover" (Exodus 12:11). Both eating in haste and eating with shoes on belong to readiness, so that, strengthened by the food, they might be able to travel. So let the one who is traveling be shod, and let the one who has reached the holy land take his shoes off. For it says, "Take off the shoe from your feet, for the place where you stand is holy ground" (Exodus 3:5). For this reason, let the one who is not an apostle have his feet shod with the readiness of the gospel of peace. But let the apostle no longer take shoes for the road, since he has already been made perfect and is in the place where, standing and walking, he is on holy ground, living in Christ.

"In all things taking up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to quench all the flaming arrows of the evil one" (Ephesians 6:16). Origen says: The arrows of the evil one are evil thoughts. So he will not be able even to begin to cast them into the heart when someone is covered by the shield of faith, since all the enemy's flaming arrows are quenched in it. And the one who carries the shield of faith will say, "In the Lord I have put my trust. How can you say to my soul, 'Flee to the mountains like a sparrow'? For look, the sinners have bent the bow; they have made ready arrows in the quiver, to shoot in the dark at the upright in heart" (Psalm 11:1-2). "Since I have put my trust in the Lord," he says, "how can you advise me not to stand up to the bows that sinners bend against me, and the arrows they make ready in quivers, wanting to wound the upright in heart? For look, I stand, and I do not move away, and all the flaming arrows of the evil one will be quenched any moment now."

title: Unit 7 rem close — Spirit's sword; bold speech; peace and incorruption
english: petition for all the saints, and for me" (Ephesians 6:18-19). Sound speech flows from the divine Spirit, but its opposite speaks from the earth. For "the one who is from the earth is of the earth and speaks from the earth; the one who comes from heaven is above all, and what he has seen and heard, to that he bears witness" (John 3:31-32). The word that comes from the Spirit is a sword, and that is why Paul says here that the sword of the Spirit is the word of God. For "the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword," and "piercing to the division of soul and spirit" (Hebrews 4:12), it cuts and divides. It also does its work through prayer and petition for those who pray at every time, and who pray with the spirit, as in "I will pray with the spirit" (1 Corinthians 14:15). And it does its work for those who keep watch in order to grow rich in the word of God, and who persevere in acquiring it, so that they may both help others and, by their prayers, work on behalf of those who help them. Notice also the apostle's modesty: he asks the Ephesians to make petitions for him.

"So that speech may be given to me when I open my mouth, to make known with boldness the mystery of the gospel" (Ephesians 6:19). Origen: When the mouth is opened and speech has been given, then the mystery of the gospel is made known with boldness, and no longer in proverbs and parables. As the Savior too says, "The hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in proverbs, but will tell you plainly about the Father" (John 16:25). Only the one whose heart does not condemn him can take in the word spoken with boldness, and everyone whose heart does not condemn him can. For "if our heart does not condemn us, we have boldness before God, and whatever we ask we receive from him" (1 John 3:21-22). So the one who makes the mystery known with boldness is rare, because the one who has boldness before God is rare. "For who will boast that he has a pure heart? Or who will speak boldly, claiming to be clean from sins?" (Proverbs 20:9).

"So that you also may know my affairs, how I am doing, Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, will make everything known to you. I have sent him to you for this very purpose, that he may know how things are with you and may encourage your hearts" (Ephesians 6:21-22). Since the apostle's whole life, and every act and activity of his, came about by the Word of God, with Christ living in him, he sends Tychicus to report to the Ephesians the rule of his life and the order of his actions. And it was fitting for the apostle to send Tychicus for this very purpose, so that the Ephesians might have a pattern of good conduct. They were also going to be encouraged, as they learned that what was best, and what befits an apostle, was being achieved by Paul.

"Peace to the brothers, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ" (Ephesians 6:23). Origen says: If there is any other gift given by God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ, peace is one as well. It is one of the most precious gifts, "the peace that surpasses all understanding," which "will guard the hearts" and thoughts of the saints (Philippians 4:7). It is a kind of calm and fair weather of the soul, a stranger to every storm, all unrest, and passion. Like peace, love with faith is also a gift given by God and the Lord Jesus Christ: love toward God, as it is written, "with the whole heart" and the rest, and toward one's neighbor "as oneself" (Matthew 22:37-39). Indeed, the one who has received love as a gift shows it even toward his enemies, hating no one and praying for those who mistreat him (Luke 6:28).

"Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption" (Ephesians 6:24). Some have explained loving him in incorruption as being pure from the works of corruption, and the works of corruption are those of sexual union. That is why common usage calls those who are pure from intercourse "uncorrupted," and those who have tasted intercourse "corrupted." And some, stretching the point further, have taken "If anyone corrupts the temple of God, God will corrupt him" (1 Corinthians 3:17) in this way, though they cannot do the same justice to "But each has his own gift from God, one of one kind and one of another" (1 Corinthians 7:7). But see whether every sin may be a corruption of the soul, and complete abstinence from sin its incorruption. Then those who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption would be those who abstain from every sin, and the grace of God is with all of them. As though there were some who love the Lord, but do not love him in incorruption, Paul says, "Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption."
